what_this_is: The Workshop row for the Namespace server in tools/live-namespace: the person's files on their own S3-compatible store, as MCP tools over stdio and as a WebDAV folder on a loopback port.

payload.label: Run the Namespace files server (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Serve the person's files: every name they were given, listed, read by range, written, moved, shared and released, as tools an AI calls and as a WebDAV folder Finder, a file browser or an editor mounts
payload.description: Starts the Namespace server (tools/live-namespace) over one state folder of the person's own. Mode `mcp` answers MCP over stdio: each operation of the files is a tool (list_files, find_file, read_file, read_file_span, write_file, write_file_start, write_file_piece, write_file_finish, share_file, move_names, copy_names, set_aside, put_back, queue_release, release_gone_bytes and the rest; tools/list names them all). Mode `dav` serves the WebDAV folder on 127.0.0.1 at the port in settings.json (38481 as shipped) until stopped: in Finder choose Go, Connect to Server and enter http://127.0.0.1:38481/ (macOS `mount_webdav -S http://127.0.0.1:38481/ <empty folder>` does the same). Mode `serve` is both. The names live in a record store file in the state folder (never a temporary folder); the bytes live in the person's own S3-compatible store, read by the asked range only, never whole. The store is the person's `files-store` connection: its fields reach the run on the file descriptors settings.json `attached` names (secret 3, key-id 4, bucket 5, endpoint 6, region 7) and are never printed, logged or written. A first run makes the store file from the connection's endpoint, bucket, region and key id and the key_prefix in settings.json. The WebDAV folder answers 127.0.0.1 and localhost only and refuses a request a web page sent. share_file refuses until the grant owner that mints a share link is attached (it is not part of this server).

mode.description: mcp: MCP tools over stdio. dav: the WebDAV folder, until stopped. serve: both.

state_folder.description: The person's own folder for the names (an absolute path in their home, never a temporary folder). It is made, readable by its owner only, when it is not there.

settings.description: Optional path to a settings file (account, WebDAV port and prefix, key prefix, attached fields), put after --settings where {settings} is in the command. Leave it out to use tools/live-namespace/settings.json.

output_schema.description: Mode mcp answers JSON-RPC lines on stdout; mode dav answers HTTP on the loopback port and prints nothing; a refusal ends the run with one line on stderr naming what was wrong, never a value of the connection.

needs: the person's files-store connection (an S3-compatible store: its secret, key id, bucket, endpoint and region), each field handed to the run on the descriptor settings.json `attached` names, read from the vault by name and never printed
an empty or earlier state folder in the person's home
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer. Run it from tools/live-namespace (its .cargo/config.toml builds SQLite with the scan counters the record store meters its reads by). Give the run the files-store connection's fields on the descriptors settings.json names (a here-string of each vault value, never echoed or logged). The first run builds and makes the store file. For the Finder folder, run mode dav (or serve) and connect to http://127.0.0.1:38481/ ; for an AI, run mode mcp as the AI's stdio MCP server. The state folder must be in the person's home: the record store refuses to keep names in a temporary folder.
